claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles with mean diameters of 5 nm and 15 nm can be prepared by the same laser synthesis method with narrow size distributions and uniform composition.
The proposed comparison heats the 5 nm and 15 nm samples from room temperature to approximately 1200 K under the same inert atmosphere and fixed heating rate.
Holding composition and synthesis method constant is intended to make nanoparticle size the only controlled variable.
Smaller high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have a greater surface-to-volume or surface-to-bulk atom ratio than larger particles.
An increased surface-to-volume ratio enhances local disorder and excess entropy at the nanoparticle surface.
A larger fraction of atoms in smaller nanoparticles occupy surface sites.
Surface atoms in smaller nanoparticles experience reduced coordination.
Reduced surface-atom coordination produces higher local disorder and free volume.
Enhanced surface disorder, excess entropy, and free volume lower the energy barrier for atomic rearrangements associated with premelting and melting.
Lower barriers for atomic rearrangement cause premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
The 5 nm CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will have a statistically significantly lower premelting onset temperature than the 15 nm particles.
The 5 nm CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will have a lower overall melting temperature than the 15 nm particles.
The 15 nm baseline particles are expected to have higher premelting and melting onset temperatures because of their lower surface-to-volume ratio.
The proposed size-dependent behavior should hold from approximately 5 nm to 15–20 nm.
Particles substantially larger than approximately 20 nm may approach bulk-like melting behavior.
Quantum size effects may dominate the behavior of extremely small particles.
DSC thermograms can identify premelting onset and melting peak temperatures, while in situ TEM can identify premelting through surface disordering or liquid-like layer formation.
Synthesis-induced defects and minor shape variations could influence the measured size-dependent melting-temperature shift.
